utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Good afternoon. If I could remind you of the affirmation you made at the beginning of your evidence, it still applies.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: [Witness answered through interpreter

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Borovic? Mrs. Tuma?

utterances.speaker: MS. TUMA
utterances.text: I'm sorry to interrupt but there is some information I would like to bring up at the beginning of this session, please, and that is concerning the witness. The witness unit has informed me that the witness needs to be back in his -- in Belgrade on Monday but he is most happy to come back, if so needed, later on but he has some business --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I would have thought, Mrs. Tuma, there is no prospect of his evidence going beyond today. I think I can rely on counsel getting through it all in a day. Including you.

utterances.speaker: MS. TUMA
utterances.text: No problem with me. It's more problem with the Defence team.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: No problem with anybody, Mrs. Tuma. Never any trouble with counsel.

utterances.speaker: MS. TUMA
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Borovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] First of all, I will try to remain in private session for a while and then we will be back to open session for the remainder of my cross-examination. I have arranged my questions in that way so that we wouldn't have to go in and out of private session all the time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: How long were you in the (redacted)?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-016 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was a (redacted) until or since 1991.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter is not sure which one the witness said.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But it was not something that was important to me, the (redacted). My job was more important.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Would you please be kind enough to tell us how long were you an (redacted) and then how long was it when you -- since you left the (redacted) and how many years did you spend as (redacted)?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-016 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Are you talking about (redacted) or how long was I in the (redacted).

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: How long were you (redacted)?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-016 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, 1991, if we calculate, I guess it's two years but, yeah, this is something that can be proved very easily.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: And how long were you (redacted) altogether?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-016 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Including the accelerated service years I think it was some 20 years.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: So if we look at all the information we have, it seems that after (redacted), people who have spent 17 or more years (redacted). Is it possible that you were not really successful in your (redacted) and that you were not (redacted)?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-016 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I said that this was not of interest to me. What was of more interest to me was to be promoted in this other area of work, in this other branch.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Well, were you an officer or were you this other thing? I don't want to mention your profession because we are in open session now. What was more important to?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-016 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, first of all, I was an intellectual.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Would you be kind enough to tell us briefly all the fronts that you toured?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-016 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I can tell you all of them. And they are Knin, Drnis, Zemunik, Western Slavonia, Okucani, Dragalic, Vukovar, Borovo Naselje. Then Mostar, Nevesinje, Trebinje above Dubrovnik, then Sibenik, Eastern Bosnia. I cannot remember them all, but I was at all of these places.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And can you now tell us, after how many years did you decide to talk about what according to you actually happened in Vukovar? How many years passed before you decided to do that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-016 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Four years.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Were you really in Vukovar on the 18th and the 19th of November 1991 or were you perhaps there in some other month?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-016 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was there because there are people who saw me there.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. When was the first time that you found out that the persons who are accused here in this courtroom have been indicted before The Hague Tribunal or by The Hague Tribunal? When was the first time you found out about it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-016 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I said I don't remember dates. I don't remember numbers. The only numbers I remember are my home phone number. I don't even know the number of my mobile phone, so people laugh at me about that sometimes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you know the number of your foreign currency account by heart?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-016 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I never knew it and I will probably never remember that and, however, I don't even have a foreign currency account. I only have a dinar account.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Well, you've already answered that question. Since that time, did you often see the accused on television, after the events in Vukovar?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-016 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I don't really watch television that much but I remember that I saw Major Sljivancanin at the Topcider barracks on New Year's celebration. (redacted) I remember seeing him maybe in 1992 or 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: (redacted), what profession were you in?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-016 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I wasn't really choosing my work. (redacted) That was among my jobs. Those were the sort of jobs that I did. I would have to -- well, we would have to move into private session because then I would be able to tell you.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. There is no need to move into private session. There is no need to abuse the Court. But you were actually doing some kind of private work; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-016 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Did you ask for the assistance of any NGO when you decided to move into the private sector?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-016 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I never asked for anyone's help.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Do you know Natasa Kandic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-016 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know her only from seeing her on television.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You said in your statement to the Prosecution and you repeated that before the Trial Chamber that you arrived at the hospital at the very moment when the evacuation of the Croatian soldiers had begun; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-016 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: And you said that this was in the early afternoon hours. Was this around 1300 hours?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-016 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the early afternoon hours. That is a little bit difficult to specify but it was sometime between 13 and 1400 hours.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Well, if it was between 13 and 1400 hours and if we add all the time period that you described here and you said that at 1600 hours you met up with your friend again, is that consistent with the scenario, at least the time frame of the scenario that you described here?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-016 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was no scenario. I visited very few places between the hospital and the other places I went at 1600 hours. I moved in a limited area.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: All right. So movements of yours, when you went to the Danube, that's several kilometres away, then you talked to your friends and then you talked to the representatives of units that you had come across. All of that took place within two hours?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-016 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. You got some things confused. You confused the two days. I went from the hospital to the park where I saw the corpses that I described, and then I went back to the workers' hall and on that day that were all of my movements.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You said that at the entrance you saw two members of military police?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-016 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were not standing at the entrance. They were standing behind the first glass door.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: How did you know if they were behind the glass door through which you didn't go, as you said to us yesterday? How did you then know that they were military police members?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-016 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Borovic, one can see that. They were clearly visible.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you have an impression that the workers were issuing orders to military policemen? You were there then, weren't you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-016 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wasn't interested in it then and I had no impression about it at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The transcript does not reflect the name Radic or do we need the witness to repeat it or can my word be sufficient in order to correct the transcript?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: That will be enough, Mr. Radic -- Mr. Borovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Was the observer from the ICRC issuing any orders to the soldiers there based on what you saw?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-016 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, Mr. Borovic. The observer just stood there as a statue looking at the entrance of the hospital. He never moved.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. These soldiers, were they armed or not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-016 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The soldiers were armed.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. At any point in time, did they go outside while were you there or not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-016 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They did not come outside. They only held the door open for the soldiers who were carrying the wounded outside.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Those who were carrying the wounded outside, were they also military policemen?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-016 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's hard to say. I was unable to see that. I just saw the soldiers carrying wounded.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: What about the other two? You said the other two who were clearly visible at the glass door. You were able to see that they were military policemen?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-016 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Radic --

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: I'm not Mr. Radic.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-016 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I apologise to you and to Mr. Radic, Mr. Borovic. Usually it is the military policemen who are present in such situations. I know my work enough in order to define that.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: So you can't claim with full certainty that those were indeed military policemen, nor do you know to which unit they belonged?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-016 [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I have already said to you, I was not interested in that at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Sir, can you tell us what were you interested in at the time? What were you looking for there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-016 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Borovic, I was interested in the event. I was interested in the wounded, in the prisoners, in the arm and in the bandages.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-016 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was quite sufficient. Surely you don't think that I was supposed to enter the hospital and question Dr. Bosanac.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. But how on earth did you find out, did you learn, that those were Croatian prisoners of war? And you ended there, you found yourself there, just out of the blue? So how were you able to determine that this was an evacuation of the prisoners?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-016 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I deduced this logically.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. How did you know that those were Croatian soldiers?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-016 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Borovic, I assumed that.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. When did you speak to Radic -- or, rather, when you spoke to Radic, did you have an official attitude or just a friendly attitude? Because allegedly you were acquaintances.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-016 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know whether he recognised me, but I always have that type of attitude.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Was your attitude an official one or a friendly one?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-016 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I greeted him in the normal way.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. It is clear that you do not wish to answer. My next question.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to have document 0053-1257 shown on the screen, page 2 of that document, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Can you see that on the screen? No, I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can this be removed from the screen for a minute, please? Just briefly, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Before you start pointing the things in the photograph, would you please describe to us the Vukovar Hospital as it looked at the time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-016 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm telling you, Mr. Borovic, that I approached it from the side that to me looked like the in your part of the hospital. So there was a path leading there.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Excuse me, as you were approaching the hospital, did you see what the hospital looked like?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-016 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I walked straight. I was in a new area, new environment. That was the first time I was there. So I went to the place that had been pointed out to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Did you see how many storeys the building had or rather did it have any storeys?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-016 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The new building had a ground floor and another floor or two.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Do you suppose there or did you see this?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-016 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw this. Of course, I saw this. I knew that the building looked new without --

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: You mean it looked as a building that used to be new before the destruction?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-016 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I mean the building looked new, and I only looked at that building. I wasn't interested in other buildings.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now have the photograph on the screen, please. Number 2, please. Thank you. That's the photograph.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Would you now be so kind and tell us -- but first please take a red marker. The usher will assist you. Thank you. Can you please draw in the direction from which you approached the hospital?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-016 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Borovic, this is a peacetime photograph.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: My question is, is this what the hospital looked like in terms of its size and physical appearance?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-016 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The part that I saw from one side looked like this.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: All right. If that is the case, would you then please slowly mark the direction from which you approached the hospital.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-016 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm telling you that that was the first time I had ever visited Vukovar. And if I were to see this site as it looked at the time, then yes, I would be fully certain, and now I will have to do some guessing. So please don't expect me to be fully accurate, because this photograph shows the hospital in a different light, so to speak.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: All right. So from which street did you approach the hospital?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-016 [Resumed]
utterances.text: From the street leading to the workers' hall. That means that I came from the direction of the MUP building. If I were able to see the MUP building here in this photograph then I would be able to be much more accurate.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mrs. Tuma?

utterances.speaker: MS. TUMA
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. The witness said that this picture has been taken in peacetime so for the Defence sake to inform the witness when the photo has been taken then so he can make a correct marking, so to say.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I think it's fair to say that we understand the photograph was taken in 1957 after reconstruction of the hospital. 1997. So that you are correct that it was a peacetime photograph but otherwise, Mrs. Tuma, I think the witness is making his position quite clear.

utterances.speaker: MS. TUMA
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Borovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: In order not to confuse you, let me put my question in these terms. You said that the size wise and the appearance wise, this is what the hospital looked like at the time. So would you please now try to describe from which direction you approached the hospital?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-016 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm doing my best. I'm trying as hard as I can, Mr. Borovic, but there are trees here.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. So you can't show that to us. My second question is: Can you show to us where the MUP building was in relation to the hospital?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-016 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The MUP building -- well, once again I have to tell you I don't know where it begins and where it ends so if the MUP building was here --

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Don't use your fingers to show the direction in the air to us. Please use the photograph.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-016 [Resumed]
utterances.text: You are asking the impossible of me, Mr. Borovic. I know where things were or the buildings were when I was there but to show it now on this photograph --

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. All right. So you are unable to show to us where in relation to the hospital was the MUP building, in front of which you parked, yes or no?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-016 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can tell you that looking from here, it was to the left.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: What you're now pointing with your hands is absolutely of no assistance to us. Your Honours, you are right. I am interrupting the witness but I need him to start marking it on the photograph, not pointing it in the air?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... Mr. Borovic. Sit down, please, Mrs. Tuma. The witness has made clear that he cannot orient himself on this photograph, that he needs to see the very building you're now asking him to mark, the MUP building, before he can decide from which direction he approached the hospital. He's indicated to you the name of a street that he used but, beyond that, he can't tell us more. So there is no point in trying to get him to mark the position of the MUP hospital when he doesn't know it.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours. Could we please show the witness photograph number 3?

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Do you see the picture now?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-016 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Can you show us on this photograph the street from which you approached the hospital?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-016 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just give me a bit of time, please. Let me rewind the tape in my head, please. No. I can't recognise that area from which I approached the hospital.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: All right. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In that case, I will have to delete a large number of questions, since you can't recognise the area.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-016 [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I saw authentic photographs, and if I could see the photographs showing the hospital from all sides, then, yes, I would be able to orient myself.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: All right. Yesterday you said that you climbed some steps and got to the glass doors; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-016 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I climbed the two steps which were not very high, but high enough for me to see the hall in the hospital.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: But you said that you didn't enter the hospital and didn't know who was there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-016 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw Major Sljivancanin at the end of the corridor.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Did you see any other officers except for the two we mentioned? And did you recognise any of them there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-016 [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean in the hospital?

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: I meant precisely what I asked, there at the spot.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-016 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't see anybody else except for those whom I have described.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: All right. So we have two men there, Sljivancanin and Radic, and nobody else; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-016 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, we have the monitor who was 30 metres away, as the crow flies. We have two nurses who passed by next to me, Radic, and Sljivancanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: I didn't ask you about the nurses because they do not fall into the category of soldiers or officers. That's why I didn't ask you about them. You say that you parked by the MUP building. Did you see a sign saying, "MUP, Vukovar"?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-016 [Resumed]
utterances.text: We were told by the soldiers we met there that.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Can you please describe the MUP building?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-016 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've already told you that that was an older building, a solid one. I think it had a ground floor and two storeys. It was a long building. It was quite bullet-ridden with broken windows. The cars that were around it were also completely bullet-ridden.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: But it was in a solid shape except for being bullet-ridden?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-016 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's how it impressed me at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you please tell the Court and tell me, of course, what was the distance between this building and the entrance outside which you lingered?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-016 [Resumed]
utterances.text: If it's true what they told me at the time, that this was the MUP building, then it wasn't too far from where I was standing. But in situations like these, you don't think in terms of distances. It struck me as being quite nearby, though.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Could you please make an effort and try to assess the distance, in terms of time and in terms of metres, perhaps?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-016 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm doing my best, really, but, once again, I must tell you that I can speak about things that I'm not certain about or at least I can't be very specific.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Well, that's an answer, too. Thank you. Near the workers' hall or the MUP building did you notice any other important buildings nearby?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-016 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I noticed the bank that is were across the way from the workers' hall. I assume they were banks because there were people's savings account books strewn all over the street.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry for interrupting you. I asked whether you saw anything near the hospital. So was this near the hospital?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-016 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No that was across the way from the workers' hall, near the Dunav hotel.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: What about near the hospital, only the MUP building? No other buildings, nor were you told about any other important buildings being near the hospital?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-016 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Borovic, I asked what I wanted to know, things I wasn't interested in were things that I didn't even ask about.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. What about the condition of the other buildings around the hospital? Is this perhaps something you noticed or not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-016 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, in my job, you use a lot of help from different sources and it's very difficult to say.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: So you don't have an answer?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-016 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I told you what the situation was that I was facing.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: What about those prisoners? At least you said they were prisoners and now you no longer seem certain. You said they were rather good-looking, nice and neat blue pyjamas with lovely stripes that were bright?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-016 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: So they were clean-shaven, their pyjamas nicely ironed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-016 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, let's not push it too far. They were clean-shaven. That much is true.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Based on your information that you had brought along (redacted)

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Did you know that at the time, Vukovar had no electricity, no running water?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-016 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I knew about some of those, but on account of the pace of my work, I simply had no time to follow everything that was going on. I believe you understand what I mean.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Those young men, where were they accommodated? Perhaps in the ambulances, the military ambulances?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-016 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were being carried towards the military ambulances belonging to the JNA.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Can you please describe one of these military ambulances? Would that be some sort of a lorry, JNA lorry, used for medical purposes?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-016 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It looks a bit like lorries that they use for distributing bread. They are olive-drab and they have a huge red cross on them.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Well, if you will allow, why did it not cross your mind that perhaps there were Serbs among those wounded? You seem to have been under the impression that all of the wounded were Croats. So why was that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-016 [Resumed]
utterances.text: You're probably not going to believe me, Mr. Borovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Probably not.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-016 [Resumed]
utterances.text: But at this moment, and at any other time when there were victims and casualties and wounded around, it just never occurred to me to think that way.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. So can you please give us zoom sort of final answer? Why did you assert in your statement that those were Croatian soldiers and prisoners on top of that? If this wasn't likely to occur to you then, well, how come that it occurred to you in 1996?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-016 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that's a bit sarcastic on your part, Mr. Borovic. I was there 15 minutes. You need to keep that in mind.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you please explain to the Chamber where those medical military ambulances were? Where did they start and where did they end?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-016 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can try to explain that. They were along that asphalt road, roughly speaking, in that general direction, parked in a line. I'm not sure how far the line extended because I'm not familiar with the layout of the place.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: But I must insist. Where did this column of vehicles begin and where did it end? You said it contained altogether about ten vehicles. Would I be right in saying that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-016 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the specific figure may vary. I didn't see the beginning but I did see the end.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: You say you didn't see the beginning. So where was the end, then, if you could tell us?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-016 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know, Mr. Borovic. I only saw the end.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Perhaps I have unduly interrupted you. You saw the end. Where was the end of the column in relation to the hospital, the tail end of the column? Do you or do you not know?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-016 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course I know, but you just wouldn't listen, would you? It was at a distance of about 25 or 30 metres from where I was standing, in that general direction. That's where the vehicles were parked.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: That direction, that general direction, can you be a bit more specific? I have no idea what you mean.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-016 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have a photograph of the environment in my mind now. Let's say I'm here and let's say I approached the place from this side, and if that's over there --

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: May I interrupt you, please? In a bid to help the Chamber, too, over there, over here, left and right, means nothing at all. Can you please be more specific in terms of the physical realities of the place? I'm sure you're capable enough of doing that for us because I think we are right now on the wrong track.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-016 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Hue can you say that I'm on the wrong track? I know exactly what I'm thinking about. I have this image in my mind. I came from this place and I was headed for this other place and to the right of where I was going is where the vehicles were parked.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. I believe that's quite sufficient by way of an answer. Are you perhaps familiar with the fact that those wounded who were evacuated from the hospital and driven off in those military ambulances, that they were eventually taken to Sremska Mitrovica, do you know that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-016 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: You say you took the main street leading to the centre of town. Do you know what the name is of that street?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-016 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I don't know its name but I know that it led all the way to the workers' hall and the plateau that I spoke about, to the right of that street, you could see the Dunav hotel.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-016 [Resumed]
utterances.text: (redacted), can we please now show Exhibit 59, and if we could please zoom in on the central part where the hospital is?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness speak closer to the microphone, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What I can see on the screen is not Exhibit 59. Can we please zoom in on the central part? Zoom in a little more, please, if possible. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: A question for the witness: How good are you at topography?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-016 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I took the subject a long, long time ago. There must be many things I've forgotten.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: I'm asking how good are you at topography. I know you took the subject as a soldier?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-016 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's true. I did, but I was never very much into it. Later on, I hardly had any opportunities to use it in practice.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Have you ever used a topographic map in practice?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-016 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Very rarely, if ever.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: If rarely, what was the last time? What would you say?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-016 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The last time must have been back in 1976.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. That should be quite sufficient for you to be able to use this particular map, shouldn't it, or are you trying to avoid answering my question?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-016 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I'm not really positive about that. I was never very much into topography.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... and I'd be pleased if you would put one and move along. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'll try.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Can you indicate the workers' hall on this map?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-016 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really -- well --

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you try to indicate location of the Dunav hotel?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-016 [Resumed]
utterances.text: You should have used a different kind of map, the one used by tourists and people who go sight-seeing.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Well, but you're not going sight-seeing are you? My next question is where is the hospital?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-016 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said I was an intellectual, not a soldier.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Well, fair enough. Okay. A question for you as an intellectual, then. Where is the MUP building in this map?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-016 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's got nothing to do with what I've just told you. What I'm telling you is that you should show me a different map. This was the first time I was in the area and you know what the extent of the destruction was at the time, don't you?

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: If I show you there arrow which says HOSP, standing for hospital, and then there is this red dot, then it appears to me that now, based on the red dot, you could show me the location of the MUP building, couldn't you?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Borovic, it doesn't matter how it appears to you. If you want to ask the question whether from this map, which is to my mind particularly unhelpful for the purpose you are trying to use it, if you want to ask him can he identify the MUP building, ask him? I'm getting very impatient at your constant use of your opinion, your interjections and your comments about the performance of the witness. That's not your role at this point. It's delaying and it's seeking to gain an upper hand over the witness. If you put a question and he can't answer it, we can appreciate that he can't answer it and will form our judgement about his performance. We don't need your comment to help us. If you would now put any questions you want about the location of buildings, but I fancy the answer you will get is no to each one of them. He can't tell you. I think that's fairly clear from his evidence so far. If you want to keep at it, go at it.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours. It is with pleasure that I will accept your criticism. As usual, you are entirely right. However, I felt that I was getting a lot of answers that were quite unclear and not too helpful for the purposes of this Court, so I allowed myself a little more liberty than usual. I apologise if I have exaggerated in that.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Could you please at least trace the route that he used on this map, the route that he took to the hospital?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-016 [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I try to use your map, Mr. Borovic, that would be an impossible feat.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: My next question: Does the witness know a person named Jovan Dulovic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-016 [Resumed]
utterances.text: From television but not personally.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: On two occasions yesterday, you said that you had seen a neuropsychiatrist, something to do with your testimony. Would you share with us the reason why you went to see a specialist?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-016 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you please repeat the question for me?

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: In answer to one of Mr. Vasic's questions yesterday, you referred to a neuropsychiatrist that you had seen. You said that this neuropsychiatrist gave you advice regarding the events that you had experienced, and what such experiences can mean for someone who is subjected to that sort of experience repeatedly. My question is: Where did you see this neuropsychiatrist, one or several, and when, the ones you mentioned yesterday?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-016 [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was only one specialist. (redacted) Only one session. I was having nightmares and I had trouble sleeping, all of which was a consequence of prolonged sojourns at the front.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Does that mean that you were receiving medication that was prescribed by there neuropsychiatrist?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-016 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I never was. I never used any medicine whatsoever. The strongest medicine I ever used were painkillers for my headache.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Which year was this when you went to consult a specialist and to receive treatment?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-016 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not receive treatment, Mr. Borovic. I went to see a doctor. That's all. I'm trying to be as specific as possible about this. I'm trying to treat you in a fair manner. I'm really trying, but I can't say the same about you, can I?

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Before we continue, we don't have you stating that you were prescribed medicine but that you refused to take it, just for the sake of transcript.

utterances.speaker: MS. TUMA
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Your Honour, but I would like the Defence counsel to reduce from comments about the witness such as "I'm trying to treat you in a fair manner, I'm really trying." Okay. That is --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: You have just --

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My apologies. I wasn't the one that was said that. I think that was something stated by the witness, not me. I apologise. As for this comment by my learned friend, this is something the witness said. I wasn't the one who said it. Let's try to be fair about this.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: So, Witness, which year was it that you went to see this specialist, a neuropsychiatrist because you had problems with nightmares?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-016 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I had difficulty with my sleeping pattern. That was the problem. That's what I meant. Can I just pause for a minute there, Your Honours, please, in order to be able to better remember what exactly what happened? Oh, yes. It was sometime in May 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. When were you prescribed this therapy that you refused to apply? You said that these were prescribed to you by a doctor and can you tell us what the therapy consisted of specifically?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-016 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have a copy with me of the medicines. It was Bensedin and some kind of mild tranquiliser; however, I never used that.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you see this specialist only once or did you go back several times and do you have medical card in relation to this type of therapy?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-016 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I went back once. I think, actually, once I went back for a checkup and then if I can remember other than that one time and the checkup, I didn't go back any more.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: And when was the first time that you talked to the psychiatrist in 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-016 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it was the first time in 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: When in 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-016 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember the exact date.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Was that the period when you were going to the front or was that already all over by then?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-016 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really don't remember. I would have to look at my records or the documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And now, can you freely provide a statement or are you suffering from any problems?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-016 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I'm not suffering from any problems. Fortunately, it all concluded very well, and before I came here to The Hague to testify, I went for a medical checkup. The company that I worked for sent me for this checkup and the doctors were quite satisfied with my state of health in relation to my age. So I was at this medical checkup a few days ago.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Well you say that you have your medical papers about this treatment with you. If it's not too indiscreet would you be willing to show them to me?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-016 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, no, I don't have them here with me, I have them at home.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Well, all right. That's sufficient. Thank you very much. You said that you were initiating proceedings in Strasbourg because of the events in the JNA. If offered, (redacted) (redacted)? At least that's what it says in the complaint.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-016 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I actually talked to the lawyer who is preparing these documents only on the telephone. This is something that is also new in our practice. I don't know the particulars, but we will see what we will be asking for once the lawyer looks at the case. I'm not sure yet. It's a little bit late to (redacted). I think that probably we will be asking for some kind of financial compensation but I don't know what will happen.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: If I understood you properly in your indictment at the Strasbourg court you're going to ask for financial damages for what had happened to you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-016 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, somebody has to pay because of what has been done to me, and that will probably be the state that will pay.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think that at this point I'm going to finish my cross-examination of this witness, Your Honours. Thank you very much?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Borovic. This is probably a practical time then for a break so that you could have a clean start. There have been redactions so it will be ten past four.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic -- oh, Mr. Bulatovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. We've made the switch because we are going to be using the technology so we have to be in this Bench, at this Bench.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: You've been promoted to the front bench.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: I'm attorney Bulatovic, the co-counsel for Major Sljivancanin, and I'm going to be asking you questions. I would like you to pay attention to the warnings made by my colleagues before, to avoid any misunderstandings and to make it easier for the interpreters to do their job properly, for your sake and for our sake, too.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I will try to go into private session as rarely as possible. I believe that that's -- enough time has been spent in private session already and I will try to direct my questions in such a way that this will not jeopardise the identity of the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: The first question is, if the witness could explain to me (redacted)? What conditions does a person need to meet? Are there any conditions, and if there are, what are they, in order to become (redacted)? And if the witness could please explain what kind of an (redacted) (redacted)?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-016 [Resumed]
utterances.text: (redacted) is someone who responded to an advertisement (redacted). They have to pass medical checks and some other tests and, if a person passes all those tests, then they will be admitted. It's an institution of higher learning. It takes four years to complete this education. Perhaps after two years the students can decide which branches they will specialise in, and they choose that according to their affinities. That's all I can say.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please tell us when does the school year begin at the (redacted)?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-016 [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I can remember, the first year begins sometime in -- well, on the 15th of September, but it doesn't necessarily have to be that date.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Once you go through all of these requirements that are necessary in order to be admitted to the (redacted) what happens and how long does it take to go through this process?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-016 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, (redacted)

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Is there a list of those who are admitted after that to the (redacted) and, if so, after how long is this (redacted)

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-016 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The (redacted) perhaps 20 days or so, after this process. It depends when a person was admitted to the (redacted)

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: In order to apply for a place at the (redacted), as you explain it, what education has to be completed before that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-016 [Resumed]
utterances.text: A person needs to complete high school, mostly people would complete the gymnasium. There were also people who graduated from some technical high schools, while those who graduated at the school for economics would go to the quartermaster school.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Is there a school for (redacted) which would have the same rank as a high school?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-016 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. There (redacted) There are also (redacted) (redacted) and, once a person completes a (redacted), they can be recruited or they can be educated as (redacted) of certain specific (redacted).

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Did you complete any of these schools for (redacted) (redacted) before you were admitted?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-016 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I graduated in the classic gymnasium.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Were there any students of the (redacted) who had previously completed the school for (redacted) and then came to the (redacted)?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-016 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that in my generation, there were no such cases.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know the reason for that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-016 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, no, I don't. I really am not able to give you any kind of answer about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: During the schooling, which took a certain amount of time, did you want to find out why there were no such persons, if there were no such persons in your class?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-016 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I personally wasn't interested in finding out the reason why.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: You talked about the academy building, nice weather, windows, reception area, telephone booth and so on. I'm interested to know how far the school building, the academy building is from the reception area?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-016 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it depends where you are looking at it from.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: If we are looking at it from the reception area?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-016 [Resumed]
utterances.text: From the reception area to the first windows, it's a distance of about perhaps 100 metres as the crow flies.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Are you familiar with the Bajnica camp museum?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-016 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Is it somewhere in the vicinity?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-016 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It's part of the academy and the school for land forces compound.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: In relation to the reception area where is it located?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-016 [Resumed]
utterances.text: In location -- in relation to the reception area, it's below the building which is actually part of the school.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: And this telephone booth, where is it in relation to the reception area?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-016 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it depends. If you go from the exit or from the entrance.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please, for the counsel.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Excuse me, we are not talking about the entrance and the exit. What I would like to know is that is it outside of the military academy compound, outside of those buildings, the academy, the dorm, and so on, or is it in the academy compound?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-016 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, this is a more precise question. It's within the compound, on the left side from the duty officer's room.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Am I to understand that this was in an enclosed area?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-016 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. It wasn't in an enclosed area. It was out in the open.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Can you please explain how was it when we are talking about it being as part of the duty officer's room?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-016 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the telephone booth is on the corner of that building.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Is that the telephone booth -- I mean, does the telephone -- is the telephone installed within a booth or not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-016 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's that old system where you insert coins. It's a large telephone booth.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: I'm not talking about how you would use it in order -- how -- what you would do in order to be able to use it. I'm just asking whether it's part of a -- within a building, whether it's under some kind of roof or under an awning or outside.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-016 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was under an awning.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: You say that in your work, (redacted)

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: (redacted). Can you please tell me what (redacted) and, as part of your work that you undertook certain steps?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-016 [Resumed]
utterances.text: (redacted)

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Let me ask you this: Did you ever hear of the command staff school for tactics?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-016 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Certainly, I did. I even know where it is located.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: I don't doubt that you as an (redacted) have to know about its location but what I'm -- would like to you do is to describe that school for us.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-016 [Resumed]
utterances.text: These schools, which are part of (redacted)

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: All right. Can you tell us how come you only (redacted) about these (redacted) when, as you told us yourself, you were an expert in your work, a very competent professional who received a lot of praise was commended many times, served in a (redacted), had a (redacted), so can you explain to us, then, why is it that you never (redacted) about the (redacted), then?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-016 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is quite simple to explain that. The education at that level is a regulated procedure, especially the graduation procedure. There is a certain protocol that needs to be followed.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Sir, I asked you for a specific answer and you gave it to me. Please do not interrupt me while I'm speaking. And I'm saying this for your sake, not for my sake. You gave us an explanation about why, within your work, you did not cover the (redacted) for tactics. You said that there was a certain protocol involved in graduation ceremonies and so on. I'm interested in this: In your work, did you learn about what kind of a school it was, what officers were eligible to attend it and what requirements they had to meet in order to be able to attend this school, to enroll in it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-016 [Resumed]
utterances.text: If this is not something that one is interested in, then one doesn't need to know about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Please, let us not waste our valuable time. All I'm asking you is: Do you know or do you not know? If you do, then explain. If you don't know, then that's fine. And then I will ask you how come you don't know, you, a person who held a high office in a very reputable centre involved in these kinds of matters.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-016 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course I know this, Mr. Bulatovic. In 90 per cent of the cases, this school was attended by professionals, officers, people who had previously command posts and were given the highest possible assessment, and were expected to have a prosperous career following that. So, yes, I know who attended that type of school.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Did you yourself ever apply to enroll into that school?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-016 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I was absolutely not interested in that.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know what rank applicants to that school had to have in order to enroll in it, the lowest rank?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-016 [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, and as far as I can remember, major or lieutenant colonel. I think a major could enroll in that school and that there were also many lieutenant colonels there.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Could somebody enroll in that school with a rank of captain?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-016 [Resumed]
utterances.text: During the period of time that I'm familiar with, that wasn't possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, can we briefly go into private session, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Private.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are in open session, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Yesterday, and today as well, you spoke about your citizenship. You said that you hold the citizenship of Serbia and Montenegro; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-016 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: I will ask you now when did you acquire that citizenship and on what basis?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-016 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was in 1997.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: On what basis?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-016 [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the basis of the time spent in the territory of Serbia and Montenegro.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Yesterday my colleagues asked you something about the reorganisation of the Yugoslav People's Army, namely when it was transformed into the Yugoslav army. There was a rule then that nobody could be an officer of the Yugoslav army unless they were citizens of Serbia and Montenegro.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-016 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's not true.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: All right. What I just told you about, was that perhaps one of the reasons that (redacted)?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-016 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's not true.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know how the officers of the Yugoslav People's Army were assigned to different duties, those who did not have the citizenship of Serbia or that of Serbia and Montenegro, and how that was done after the JNA ceased to exist and the Yugoslav army was founded?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-016 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I only know about the cases that are similar to mine, those who had the same fate as I did, namely all of these people left the JNA.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: When you gave evidence, you mentioned a man who hailed from Karlovac, whose name was Zdenko Urisk. You said that he was a warehouseman. Would you please explain to me and everybody else what type of contacts you had with him, where he worked as a warehouseman, in what facility?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-016 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was a chance meeting in front of the military schools' centre. We just greeted each other. He was a Lieutenant Colonel, a very capable officer. I know what posts he held earlier, because we were of the same age. He asked me about my work, and I told him, and he said that he was not -- he didn't have a proper job but, rather, was assigning beds and blankets and so on to the refugees and so on.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: That was the military schools centre. Where did it exist? Within what type of institution?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-016 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was a special, independent institution which had within it this staff command school for tactics and some other high military schools. There was also the national defence school and a political school there.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: All right. Did this centre exist within the General Staff?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-016 [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, they were a separate, independent institution, but most likely, just like everybody else, they were under the command of the General Staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: If I were to tell you that this individual that you mentioned, Zdenko Urisk, in 1996, worked in the military schools centre, would you agree with me?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-016 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not without verifying certain things. I would have to talk to the man.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: When you talked to him, and when he told you that he worked as a warehouseman, when did this conversation take place?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-016 [Resumed]
utterances.text: This conversation took place -- all I could tell you was that it was during the time when the families of the officers started arriving and they were housed in the dormitories of officers who were students of those schools. I know that it was that period of time but I couldn't be more specific.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Can you remember what year it was?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-016 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not really, Mr. Bulatovic. All I can do is speculate and I don't like to do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Was that before your service was terminated? Let us see if we can find a reference point. Was that while you still worked or after you had stopped working or several years after that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-016 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think this was after I had stopped working. Definitely after, because I remember saying to him how it had all transpired with me.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: All right. I will now tell you that based on the information that I saw while preparing for this, Zdenko Urisk worked in the main library of the military schools as one of deputy heads of the library. He was a major and he was assigned to a post corresponding to his rank. In 1998, when reorganisation of military educational schools was conducted, he was promoted to the post of a scholar, a researcher, and that that was within -- and that this was within this institution. Would you say that this isn't true, what I just told you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-016 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I could certainly trust you blindly, but I'm telling you that I did meet Zdenko and that, at the time, this is the job that he had. I don't know what happened to him afterwards.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Will you please tell me now how you came to meet him and to hold this conversation with him, that type of conversation?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-016 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Would you please clarify your question? Could you be more specific?

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: I will try to, even though you as an educated man, simply refuse to understand certain things. So this is what I'm saying. You're meeting a man whom you basically don't know. You're meeting him for the first time and all of a sudden you start talking about to him about some very private matters, from your private life. I want to know is how could you trust somebody whom you knew so very briefly at the time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-016 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Bulatovic, you have to be specific. Which man do you have in mind? You're saying you were talking to a man. Which man? And I'll give you an answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: So far, I have mentioned only one man with whom you had talked. His name is Zdenko Urisk. I hope you didn't forget it in the meantime.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-016 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Bulatovic, you have to understand that this is the third day that I'm working under pressure, psychological pressure, and it is quite natural for my concentration to drop. (redacted)

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: In that case, we misunderstood each other. That is possible. So after this conversation you never saw him again?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-016 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I never saw him again.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, can we go into private session, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Private.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are back in open session, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: To go back now to the main events, to the events of Vukovar, there was quite a lot of vagueness and misunderstanding in your answers so I wanted to maybe avoid that, go into that. In your statement that you gave to the Prosecution, it says as follows: I'm not going to give it to you to read so that we can save sometime. I'm going to read it to you and, if you have any doubts about whether it really says that or not, then, of course, I'm going to give you the document for you to look at. I'm reading from the B/C/S version. "I arrived at Vukovar in the morning, on the 18th of November 1991, a day when -- that was the day the fighting stopped between the JNA and the Croatian army. That is where I stayed until the 20th of November 1991." Today in response to a question by my learned friend Mr. Borovic you talked about something else. You said something else. You said that on the 20th you were in Sombor. That is why I would like to ask you to explain to me, and we'll go in order, your movements first of all, when you left Belgrade to get to Sid on the 18th or the 17th whenever you set out on the trip, when you were in Sid, to give me the time, how did you get to Vukovar from Sid and how long did the trip take. On the 18th, how long did you stay in Vukovar, and then we can end with the 19th, with your departure from the -- from Vukovar. Then we'll move to the 19th and so on because I would like to clarify somethings. There are many things that are not quite clear in these movements of yours so. I don't want anybody to misunderstand my intentions. They are quite clear.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-016 [Resumed]
utterances.text: We left Belgrade on the 18th, in the early morning. We arrived at Sid at around 11.00. We stayed there for a short while, perhaps half an hour or so. And then we continued our trip to Vukovar.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Can you explain -- can you remember perhaps which way you took?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-016 [Resumed]
utterances.text: This was my first time in that area, so I cannot give you a precise answer, but it was a regular road, route, with checkpoints and the driver had no problems. I was sitting next to the driver.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: If I understood you properly, the driver was a photo journalist who worked for some French news agency. Don't worry, I'm not going to mention the name. There are plenty of French such agencies.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-016 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct. It was his vehicle.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: And what was the make of the vehicle?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-016 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that it was a Yugo car.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: What were the licence plates on the car?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-016 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I really don't know. If I knew I would be a genius.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: You were person who was supposed to help these two people get to Vukovar as quickly as possible. Did you take with you any kind of documents? You were informed about the existence of checkpoints and that it wasn't possible just for anybody to pass through them.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-016 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course. They received passes at the press centre. I had more than that. As far as documents are concerned, so there were no problems.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: These passes at the press centre, did you have to fill in a form to receive such a pass or they were just being distributed, issued to whoever turned up?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-016 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know how the head of the (redacted) worked but we received the passes and they looked okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: According to your information and according to what you saw sitting next to the driver, was the driver a person who came to that area for the first time or was he someone who had been there before?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-016 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was the first time in that area for all of us.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: You said that you came to Sid at about 11.00. You stayed there briefly. How long?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-016 [Resumed]
utterances.text: About half an hour, enough to have some coffee and to complete the formalities.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: And when did you get to your destination?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-016 [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the early afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Could you be more specific about the time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-016 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I will try. Perhaps it was sometime around 2 p.m., early afternoon hours.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Does that mean that if you came to Sid at 11, stayed there for half an hour, then left Sid at around 11.30, and then you arrived at Vukovar at around 2 p.m.? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-016 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot give you a specific answer, but we did get there.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Very well. You answered some questions by my learned friend Mr. Borovic about reaching the Vukovar Hospital. You said that this entrance where you saw them bringing out the wounded and that was also where you saw the officers whom you mentioned, there were stairs, there was a wide asphalt road, if I understood you properly, there were a few steps. And you went up the stairs, looked inside, and you saw Major Sljivancanin. Did I understand you correctly?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-016 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, you did.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: The place where you climbed those steps, how many more steps were there in front of you in order to reach a level area? Can you perhaps tell us?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-016 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it wasn't a very long staircase, perhaps there were two or three steps more, but that was about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Does that mean that when you climbed the stairs, you came to a glass door?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-016 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Was this door open?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-016 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. The door was closed. It was probably an automatic door.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: How long did you stay there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-016 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I looked inside, noticed what I saw, then I came back. I went back.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: And tell me this. If I understood you properly, and in order to avoid any misunderstanding, through the door you saw Major Sljivancanin standing further along the corridor. How far -- how long was this corridor in relation to the place where you were standing?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-016 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it seemed to me quite a large space but if you would like me to take a guess, I think from me to the place where Major Sljivancanin and those soldiers were standing, it was some 20 metres.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Very well. And that same entrance where you were standing, as far as I understood, was the same entrance that they were bringing out the wounded from?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-016 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: And all of this was sometime in the early afternoon, around 2 p.m.?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-016 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, approximately.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: And now, this other encounter you had with Mr. Sljivancanin, which you described, this was when you were near the workers' hall, the Radnicki dom. I'm interested exactly where you were standing? Were you near the workers' hall? Were you near the hospital when you saw Veselin Sljivancanin and two escorts passing?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-016 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was in front of the statue that you can see on the photograph that we looked at.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: That was the photograph that you made on the 18th; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-016 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please tell me the entrance where we were standing and the statue or the sculpture, how far apart were they?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-016 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I cannot give you a specific answer because I was working in that time. I was working, I was using the devices that I had available. So I wasn't really noticing the distances, the space.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please wait for a second? Something here doesn't quite match up. You were leaving, you were going, you met two young girls, one with black hair, one with brown hair, they were wearing coats, you spoke with them, after that you went towards the workers' hall?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-016 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no. First I went to the park where there were the bodies of persons who died in the hospital, and they were covered.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Very well. And how long did you stay there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-016 [Resumed]
utterances.text: This was interesting and I stayed there for about half an hour.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: And then after that, you went towards the workers' hall?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-016 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Then I looked at the civilians. There was a young mother with a child and also I spent some time there.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: In relation to this first encounter -- well, let us clarify so that we don't proceed like this and waste time. In relation to the first encounter, when you saw Veselin Sljivancanin in that corridor, when he was standing some 20 metres away from you, and this other encounter, how much time passed between these two encounters, half an hour, an hour, an hour and a half?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-016 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that if this was three, something like that, I think perhaps it was an hour and 45 minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: After that, you left and then you took this photograph with these three people, which you then gave to Tribunal representatives; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-016 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Exactly where was this photograph taken? You did talk about it but I'm asking this because I have a reason for it and I will tell you what the reason is.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-016 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The photograph was taken on the pavement behind the sculpture. The plateau is -- leads in the direction of the Dunav hotel.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Is the workers' hall nearby?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-016 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I was told that the workers' hall was there on the corner.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: If I am not mistaken, when you were interviewed, you said that you found the workers' hall and that you recognised it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-016 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was the first time I saw it, and I recognised the characteristic line of the building, and then later I checked to make sure that that was it.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: So the photograph was not taken near or at the workers' hall?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-016 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The workers' hall is nearby, in the key it states that it's the plateau in front of the Dunav hotel.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Which -- which key? Which caption are you talking about?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-016 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The caption on the back of the photograph, the index.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: On the back of the photograph, it says, "Across from the Dunav hotel, across the road." So I want to see what road it is that we are talking about.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-016 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that I was clear. I wanted to pinpoint that from the place where I was standing, it was across from the Dunav hotel. I think that the sentence is clear.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: The interview with the Tribunal representatives, on this topic, contains the following, (redacted)

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: that it was a sculpture there, and that we can see it on the photograph and so on.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-016 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Please, Mr. Bulatovic, this is a very small area. It's a small area. I had to relate to something.
