It's much closer, about 50 metres away, the workers' hall while the Dunav hotel is a bit further off, some 200 to 300 metres off. So you would always relate to the building that was closer.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Well, this is what I wanted to ask you about. From this point where you were standing, how far from that point is the workers' hall and how far from that point is the Danube hotel in let's clarify that.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-016 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well in my assessment but I wasn't really dealing with the distances, the workers' hall was quite close, within 100 metres, while erstwhile the Danube hotel, the Dunav hotel, was furthers away. In my estimate it was some 3 to 400 metres away. It was quite a large plateau.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Let's come back to your arrival at the hospital. When you reached the hospital and that entrance that you described, as you were moving towards the hospital, did you pass by any part of the hospital or did you reach the entrance of the hospital immediately from the road?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-016 [Resumed]
utterances.text: From that road I came directly to the hospital entrance.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Did you notice, as you were approaching the hospital entrance, that there was any kind of a sign pointing or indicating that this was a hospital?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-016 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't pay attention to such details.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: In front of the entrance, or above the entrance, did you see a Red Cross flag?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-016 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw no such flag.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Did you see any buildings across from that entrance, which looked like health services buildings? Could you conclude that based on anything?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-016 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Everything that I had within my view was that hospital.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: All right. Let us look at some other issues. You said that you saw Mr. Sljivancanin for the first time -- I don't mean Vukovar now. I just mean generally, in life. You saw him for the first time when he was a student of the military academy. Next time you saw him was in Vukovar. In between, between 1972, 1973 and 1991-1992, did you ever see him, talk to him, follow his progress, his work, or anything similar?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-016 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, naturally, during that long period of time, I saw Mr. Sljivancanin many times. Whether we had ever talked, I don't remember that.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Can you give us examples of places where you met him up until 1991?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-016 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I used to see him within the Marshal Tito barracks, which was later renamed the Topcider barracks. I used to see him during various military exercises, perhaps on some other occasions, but those were accidental meetings.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: You mentioned military exercises, manoeuvres, just a bit ago?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-016 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: You mentioned a military exercise called Pestar in which the Guards Brigade participated according to your information?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-016 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Which year was that drill, that exercise held, the one called Pestar?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-016 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can give you an approximate time-frame, between 1986 and 1989. I couldn't be more specific than that. I know it was autumn, late autumn.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know that the Guards Brigade took part -- do you know whether the Guards Brigade took part in any other drill or exercise?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-016 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I moved into another area of work, and I didn't follow these developments.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: As I understood it, you followed the developments in Territorial Defence and civilian protection. That's what you said.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-016 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did, but in a different type of a session.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Members of Territorial Defence and civilian protection, did they participate in military drills?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-016 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's a very clear issue.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Within your area of work, within this field mentioned in the certificate, society and defence, did you write any reports about the participation of Territorial Defence and civilian defence units in that drill? In other words, do you know whether in this military training -- military drill called Pestar which was held between 1986 and 1989, these units took part, the ones which you followed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-016 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not aware of that, because what I was interested in were assault units and developments, and this was the topic that I followed. And the drill, this military drill, was a huge one.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: All right. We don't have to go into details. We covered the events of your stay in Vukovar up until the 1600 hours on the 18th of November. Please tell me what happened afterwards. Did you go back to Sid?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-016 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I met up with my colleagues. We went to the end of the city, to follow the evacuation of civilians.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Who took you there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-016 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just like before, driver, co-driver, escort, and we asked about that and we got there.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: How long did you stay there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-016 [Resumed]
utterances.text: We spent -- we stayed there until the nightfall.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: And following that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-016 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Following that, we went back to Sid.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Using the same road?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-016 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was dark. I think that for a while we travelled on the same road as the convoy. We were trying to get through and it was difficult.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Did you stay long in Sid?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-016 [Resumed]
utterances.text: We spent the night there, and then on the following day, they left and I stayed on.?

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It was a trophy.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: So they didn't?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-016 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Most likely, they didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Did this permit, this pass, have a military stamp?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-016 [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was some type of a stamp on it but I remember nothing further.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: It was issued by the military, it was a military document?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-016 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But it was issued on a one-time basis for that day alone and it wasn't valid on the following day.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: All right. So it was a one-day pass?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-016 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: On the following day, on the 19th, where did you go from Sid and where -- and when?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-016 [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the following day, at around 8.00 in the morning, I went to the press centre. As I have already told you --

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: You don't need to repeat because we do not want to waste time. I have important things to ask you.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-016 [Resumed]
utterances.text: We took the shortest road to Borovo Naselje.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: And what is the shortest road?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-016 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The driver knew that. He was the one doing the driving.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: And then from Borovo Naselje, if I'm not mistaken, after everything you did there, you went and you spoke to the navy captain; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-016 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. We stayed very briefly there, perhaps an hour, and then we went back to Vukovar.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: And how long did you stay in Vukovar on the 19th and what time of the day was it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-016 [Resumed]
utterances.text: We stayed there from the afternoon -- we didn't stay very long and then we went back.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Where?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-016 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Towards Sombor. I think we travelled via Backa Palanka.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: When did you speak to the navy captain?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-016 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was in the early afternoon hours.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: On the 19th?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-016 [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the 19th.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: On the 20th of November, you were not in Vukovar?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-016 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I was not. I was some place else.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: All right. You keep mentioning this other place where you were. What was it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-016 [Resumed]
utterances.text: We went to visit a unit of air defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: I'm interested in the location. I am into the interested in military issues such as which type of a unit and so on. What place was it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-016 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sombor.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: You said that that was 40 kilometres from Vukovar.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-016 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. First we visited that and then we went there.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Would you please explain what is "that" and what is "there"?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-016 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was another air force unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: And where was that unit, in what town?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-016 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't pay attention because that was not my area of work.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Then why did you go there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-016 [Resumed]
utterances.text: To accompany somebody else and because I had transportation.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: And when did you return to Belgrade?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-016 [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the 20th, in the evening.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Would you tell me, please, your next visit to Vukovar came how long afterwards?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-016 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not quite sure, but on that occasion, we also had a vehicle and there were several of us.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Was there a specific reason for your trip, your return trip, to Vukovar?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-016 [Resumed]
utterances.text: We toured some places. (redacted)

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Borovic asked you to describe the location of the MUP building in relation to the hospital, the distance and so on, and you were unable to show that on the photographs and on the maps shown to you. I will not go back to that but I will try to rephrase that question. Since you covered that distance on foot from the MUP building where you parked to the hospital, you said that that was nearby, and now I'm interested in the distance between the hospital and the Dunav hotel. Can you estimate that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-016 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Bulatovic, I already attempted to do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Well, just roughly. I fully appreciate your efforts. Can you be more specific?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-016 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. And I don't like to speculate.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: You gave evidence and said that you discussed with your colleagues and then you said, "I don't know how to say this in English," but you said that Sljivancanin went on and on and on in his conversation with the representative of the International Red Cross.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-016 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's precisely what I said.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: I will ask you whether that was the same ICRC representative as the one we saw in front of the hospital?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-016 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Based on what I saw, yes, that's the same man, the same representative as the one on television.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: That was on the 18th, when you saw the representative, the same man, in front of the hospital. On that wall, that was just two or three metres high?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-016 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: And you said that you recognised him because two or three evenings prior to that, you watched his -- him arguing with Veselin Sljivancanin?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-016 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I saw that on television.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: All right. And you saw that two or three evenings prior to that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-016 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: And where was that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-016 [Resumed]
utterances.text: At home.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: All right. So you were at home with the people who live in your house and, on that occasion, you commented about Sljivancanin going on and on and on. You didn't comment on that when talking to your colleagues?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-016 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's not true. That conversation took place in our office.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, is this good time for a break?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It is, Mr. Bulatovic. There have been and there will be another redaction and we will resume -- Mrs. Tuma?

utterances.speaker: MS. TUMA
utterances.text: Sorry, Your Honour, but just one question, please. It's concerning the planning of the next witness, if the Court intends -- I don't know how long this cross-examination will take.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Can you assist us at all, Mr. Bulatovic? I realise you've been going very efficiently.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I think another 45 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: That gives you five minutes, Mrs. Tuma. Is that enough?

utterances.speaker: MS. TUMA
utterances.text: That's enough for me, yes, I think so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Try to make it 40 minutes, Mr. Bulatovic. In that event, there will be another witness on Monday. On Monday, we are sitting in the afternoon and then the rest of the week we sit in the morning.

utterances.speaker: MS. TUMA
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Then we must adjourn now and with the redactions it will be half an hour, so ten past six.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Bulatovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, thank you. Can we please go into private session, briefly?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Private.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are back in open session, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Can you please tell us the location of the Guards Brigade barracks?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-016 [Resumed]
utterances.text: What do you mean? Of course, I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Briefly, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-016 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Topcider.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know about the Guards hall or centre?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-016 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I know that too. It's within the perimeter of the barracks.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: If I tell you that the Guards Brigade barracks is at Trebinje and has nothing whatsoever to do with the barracks at Topcider, would you tend to agree with me on that one?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-016 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I will agree with you because we use the term in a very general way.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You spoke about some sort of ethnic cleansing, of which you, too, were a victim. You spoke about the anti-terrorist platoon. Are you familiar with the following names, the first one being Vehid -- Fehid Karavelic, a Muslim person?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-016 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: What about the name of Adem Becirevic, another Muslim?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-016 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: You spoke about that person you met, I'm not sure what you called him, I think you called him Razvigor. What about the last name of Dirijevic [phoen]? Does that ring a bell?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-016 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not right now.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: You said you met this man called Razvigor at one of the youth meetings or work meetings?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-016 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell me which meeting or which operation -- youth work operation and which year?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-016 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said I can't be very specific about that, and it's not my style to speculate.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: If speculation is not your style, can you please again repeat for me your description of this man named Razvigor, when you saw him on that motorbike in Vukovar? What was he wearing? Was he wearing a beard, perhaps, a close description?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-016 [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was wearing a civilian jacket, military trousers, and he was not wearing a cap.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: I would now like to ask you to look at a very brief portion of footage and please confirm if this is the man named Razvigor who you saw at Vukovar. Please have a look now.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: This person on the motorbike that you can see in this footage, is that Razvigor?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-016 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Looks nothing like the man I know.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Brief question: When you're off on a mission, you have your camera, you said you had a Nikon with a colour film, and a Praktica containing a black and white film. Do you sign for these things, such as cameras and film rolls when leaving, and do you have to account for these items once back?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-016 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I only signed for the film rolls.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Who checks this, whether you're using your own film rolls or those that you previously signed for?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-016 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Never occurred to us to use our own film rolls.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: My question is not about whether it occurred to you but, rather, were you able or were you in a position or would you have been allowed to use your own?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-016 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, in theory. It's just that I myself never did that.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Okay. You were given a task, as you said, as you testified in chief, on the 23rd of November 2005, a specific task. My colleague Borovic showed you this and I'm going to show you what you said on the 23rd of November 2005. (redacted)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It does, I think, need to be in private session, Mr. Bulatovic. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are in open session, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Did you see the video now?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-016 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Are these the bodies that you saw?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-016 [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I arrived, those bodies were covered by canvas or tarpaulin. I think the bodies had probably been moved in the meantime.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Do you recognise the general environment so to speak? Are these the bodies that you saw covered by tarpaulin?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-016 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It looks like the same environment that I came across but the question is were the bodies moved in the meantime.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Okay. Let me ask you, when you saw the bodies, did you in any way try to ascertain who had committed this crime? You saw the types of injuries that could be seen, right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-016 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Under those circumstances, that would have been impossible.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I move that this be admitted into evidence, the footage that we have just shown. This is a video clip that we received from the OTP, and the number is V0001170-1-A.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This will be Exhibit 116, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: In order to move on to that bit where Sljivancanin was being a pain in the neck, the substance of that conversation that you heard in the house and what you heard from your colleagues at work, can you tell us the substance? Try to paraphrase or if you know the exact course of the conversation.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-016 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was a long time ago. I remember exactly when he spoke to the representative of the International Red Cross saying stuff like, "Sir, this is my country." That sort of thing. I can't remember all the details. We believed he took an arrogant approach and was being very arrogant to this poor man who was only there to help us and we in the (redacted) had our comments. We were saying things like, well, okay there were people who approved of that but --

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: But the substance of the conversation, in addition to what you said, sir, "this is my country," was there anything else that Sljivancanin said?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-016 [Resumed]
utterances.text: You're really asking a lot.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: To the best of your recollection?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-016 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well to the best of my recollect, he said, "Sir, this is my country. I -- these are our own problems." I can't just say off the back like that without speculating. What I didn't like about it was the arrogance that he displayed. I think he should have found a more diplomatic way of going about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: So that seems to be the only problem.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-016 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I have a personal dislike for arrogance, for arrogant behaviour. I think a diplomatic approach is much better, as a rule.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: You saw that for a -- three or four days before you went to Vukovar on the 18th?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-016 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know how many days before but I did see it. It was on the news.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Did you after that saw -- did you after that see any other video showing Sljivancanin talking to that representative of the International Red Cross, the same one that you saw near the hospital on the 18th?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-016 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Bulatovic, the nature of my job entailed a lot of travel. Very often we didn't have time to read papers or watch TV.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Could I ask my learned friend something? In order to refresh the witness's memory, I will show you something, some footage, with the sound, this is the conversation between the International Red Cross man and Mr. Sljivancanin. Before that, please tell me one thing. Was there anyone else there, any other officers in addition to Veselin Sljivancanin? Were there any other soldiers in the vicinity. What about this representative of the International Red Cross. Did he have a deputy? Was he with someone? Is this something you remember?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-016 [Resumed]
utterances.text: There is just a very short clip that was shown on TV. It's hard to remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: You said a very short clip. Can you specify how long he was going on like that in terms of time and on and on and on until the cows came home, as you said?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-016 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it's difficult for me to specify but it did go on for quite sometime.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please play the video? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Is this the same video that you saw two or three evenings before you left for Vukovar on the 18th?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-016 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I would like to tender this into evidence, please, this video. Again it was obtained from the OTP, the number is V0001231-1-A.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This will be Exhibit 117, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I'm about to play another video, if that's all right. It has to do with this conversation, and this will complete my cross-examination of the witness. Therefore, can we now please play the next video?

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Do you see this frame?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-016 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Is that part of the same footage that you saw earlier?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-016 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I didn't watch this part.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Are these the same people? Is it the same location, the same time, the same place?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-016 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I was paying more attention to the actual conversation than to the surroundings.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Can you read what it says on the caption on that footage?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-016 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It states Vukovar, the 20th of November, 1991.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Do you see a sign in the top right corner of this frame?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-016 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: And what is that sign or logo?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-016 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you please focus in or zoom in on it?

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Unfortunately, we are not able to do that. We can try. Can you try now as we are playing the footage, if you can see?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-016 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it's something like RTS, RTS, it's the TV station logo.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: If it says RTS, do you know what the RTS stands for?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-016 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Radio-television Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: And is it perhaps RTB?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-016 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Then it's Radio-television Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: This news programme that you saw, was that perhaps broadcast by RTB, Radio-television Belgrade, by that television station?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-016 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I think that that was the name of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please move into private session now?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Private.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: And yes, that will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are in open session, Your Honour. And the Exhibit will be number 118.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I have finished my cross-examination. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Bulatovic. Mrs. Tuma?
